recommendation_reason: Rewrite A (phi4) better aligns with the job listing’s emphasis on practical repair skills, customer service with older patrons, and reliability. It explicitly mentions explaining technical concepts without jargon, a key requirement, and directly ties the candidate’s experience to the role’s needs. While both rewrites passed fact-checks, Rewrite A’s structured format and targeted language (e.g., ‘high-reliability and patience,’ ‘local resident’) make it more compelling for this hands-on, customer-facing role. Rewrite B’s casual tone and vague skills (e.g., ‘Microsoft Word, mostly’) feel less aligned with the job’s practical demands.

career_roadmap.step: Apply for the role with Rewrite A
career_roadmap.action: Submit the phi4 rewrite to Mick via email, emphasizing the ‘Relevance to Brenda & Mick’s’ section and practical repair experience mentioned in the skills list.
Enroll in a short-course certification program for basic PC repair (e.g., CompTIA A+ or local community college courses) to strengthen credibility for future roles.

Use this position as a stepping stone to apply for roles with higher technical complexity (e.g., IT support specialist or certified repair technician) after gaining 6–12 months of on-the-job experience.
